title: A square-zero closed immersion identifies its unit and additive kernels.
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], J ≤ I quasi-coherent ideal sheaves with I*I ≤ J [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and j: Z_I → Z_J their inclusion. Then the kernel of unit restriction q_j [def-sc-gm-torsor] is isomorphic, as an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of Z_J, to the kernel of additive restriction r_j [def-sc-etale-additive-structure-restriction], using the same coefficient universe lift. No nilpotence hypothesis on I in X is required.

proof.text: The ideal of Z_I in Z_J is I/J and has square zero. Its extension K to every affine etale Z_J-object still has square zero. Unit kernel sections are the units 1+a with a in K; additive kernel sections are a in K.
Send u to u-1, and a to 1+a with inverse 1-a. Since a*b=0 for a,b in K, (1+a)(1+b)=1+a+b. The maps are inverse group homomorphisms.

These formulas commute with all ring restriction maps and universe lifts. They define inverse natural morphisms on an affine etale basis and hence inverse morphisms of the kernel sheaves. Their composites are the identity on the basis and therefore on the sheaves. Zero ideals and the empty scheme give trivial kernels.

theorem nonempty_squareZeroRelativeUnitsAdditiveKernelIso (X : Scheme.{u})
    (I J : X.IdealSheafData) (hJI : J ≤ I) (hII : I * I ≤ J) :
    Nonempty (kernel (gmSheafToLowerStarGmSheaf (IdealSheafData.inclusion hJI)) ≅
      kernel (etaleAdditiveSheafToLowerStar (IdealSheafData.inclusion hJI)))
